question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Washout and re-challenge hysteresis assay
ideas.description: Pulse cells with a stimulus, withdraw it, and track AP-1 target gene expression over time. Memory would appear as persistent expression after withdrawal and faster or stronger re-induction on re-challenge, which should be lost in AP-1 mutants lacking DNA binding or dimerization.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the rest phase
ideas.description: Use an auxin-inducible degron on FOS or JUN to remove AP-1 after priming but before re-challenge. If AP-1 is the memory substrate, degradation should erase the primed state, while degradation before priming should prevent it from forming.

ideas.title: Chromatin persistence time course (ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, H3K27ac)
ideas.description: Profile AP-1 occupancy and enhancer accessibility and acetylation at primed and naive sites across a stimulus-withdrawal time course. This tests whether chromatin opening outlasts AP-1 binding and whether it is maintained by AP-1 itself or by a separate epigenetic mechanism.

ideas.title: Live single-cell reporter with lineage tracking
ideas.description: Express a fluorescent AP-1 target reporter, prime cells, and follow individual lineages through several divisions by time-lapse imaging. Quantify how long the primed state persists and whether it is inherited by daughter cells, and test whether mitotic bookmarking or chromatin-remodeling perturbations shorten that inheritance.

ideas.title: Feedback-loop perturbation and bistability testing
ideas.description: Disrupt candidate positive feedback loops (FOS autoregulation, ATF3 or JUN loops) and co-activator inhibition (p300/CBP or BRD4) in single-cell reporter lines. Memory should scale with loop strength and show bimodal, cell-autonomous persistence rather than a population-average decay, and this should be validated in vivo with a repeated-stimulus model.
